Action Plan:
1. Acute cough/rhinorrhea (likely viral): conservative self-care — rest, maintain hydration, regular paracetamol as needed for symptoms; avoid unnecessary exertion. Verbal advice that most viral URIs last ~7–10 days; expect improvement over next few days.
2. Review / return plan for cough: if symptoms not improving in 2–3 days, or sooner if breathing worsens or fever persists, return for re-evaluation; clinician may examine and consider further management (e.g., antibiotics if still febrile and cough not improving).
3. Work/capacity: advised to take 1–2 days off work if possible to rest; reassess ability to return early next week depending on recovery.
4. Alcohol counseling: advised to reduce alcohol intake (practical stepwise reduction suggested by clinician).
5. Medication reconciliation / monitoring: documented current regular medications (Metformin; lisinopril — dose/route/frequency not documented); no immediate change recommended during this visit.
6. Documentation/consent: Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: persistent dry cough and runny nose for ~5–6 days.
- Cough characteristics: continuous, dry, worse at night, interrupts sleep, causing throat irritation; non-productive (no sputum).
- Associated symptoms: rhinorrhea; subjective chills/feeling feverish (no temperature measured); generalized myalgias and marked fatigue/weakness; brief diarrhea at onset that has resolved; no nausea/vomiting; no ear pain/discharge.
- Respiratory: no baseline dyspnea walking around; transient breathlessness only during coughing; no chest pain.
- Past medical history: type 2 diabetes mellitus; hypertension.
- Medications: Metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented); Lisinopril (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies: none reported.
- Social history: lives with partner (partner currently asymptomatic); works as a developer (sedentary job); former smoker (stopped ~6 months ago); alcohol use: wine ~2–3 glasses on ~3 evenings/week.
- Family history: father with type 2 diabetes.

Objective:
- No formal vital signs or physical examination findings documented in transcript.
- Clinician noted audible dry cough during consult; no mucky/phlegm heard.
- Patient-reported findings: subjective shivering, myalgias, resolved diarrhea.
- No investigations were performed or reported.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute cough / viral upper respiratory infection (acute bronchitis):
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Viral upper respiratory infection / acute bronchitis (High). (DDx: "Viral upper respiratory infection / acute bronchitis (viral)" — High)
   - Differential diagnosis (consistent DDx items):
     - Influenza — Medium (DDx). Supporting: prominent myalgias, chills, marked fatigue, acute onset. Opposing: no measured high fever recorded; no abrupt severe onset documented.
     - COVID-19 — Medium (DDx). Supporting: dry cough, myalgias, subjective fever/chills, transient diarrhea. Opposing: no testing performed; no anosmia/ageusia documented; partner well (does not exclude).
     - Post-viral cough / reactive airways — listed in DDx (consistent). Supporting: cough persisting after upper respiratory prodrome.
     - ACE inhibitor–induced cough (lisinopril) — Medium (DDx). Supporting: patient takes lisinopril; cough is dry and nocturnal. Opposing: onset coincided with runny nose, systemic viral symptoms (fever/chills/myalgias) suggesting infectious cause; ACE cough more typically develops over weeks–months.
   - Investigations planned: none performed now. Plan is clinical follow-up; re-evaluate if not improving. (No specific tests were ordered in the visit.)
   - Treatment planned: symptomatic care — rest, adequate fluids, regular paracetamol as needed. Consider antibiotics only if patient remains febrile and cough not improving on re-evaluation (as discussed by clinician).
   - Referrals: none at this time.

2. Work/capacity:
   - Assessment / likely issue: reduced functional capacity from acute viral illness.
   - Differential: N/A (contextual).
   - Investigations planned: none.
   - Treatment/plan: advised to take 1–2 days off work if possible and rest; reassess ability to return early next week based on recovery. Return earlier if breathing worsens or symptoms markedly worsen.

3. Alcohol intake / lifestyle counseling:
   - Assessment / likely issue: ongoing alcohol intake at near-recommended limits; clinician advised reduction.
   - Differential: N/A.
   - Investigations planned: none.
   - Treatment/plan: clinician advised stepwise reduction in alcohol (e.g., reduce to two glasses/week initially then further reduction) given background of hypertension and diabetes.

4. Chronic conditions / medications (diabetes, hypertension, lisinopril):
   - Assessment / likely issue: stable chronic conditions under routine care.
   - Differential: ACE inhibitor cough considered above as differential for persistent cough.
   - Investigations planned: none emergent; continue routine follow-up with usual care providers.
   - Treatment/plan: no acute medication changes made during this consult. Documented current medications: Metformin; Lisinopril (dose/route/frequency not documented).

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements: no vital signs (temperature, pulse, blood pressure, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation) recorded; no focused respiratory examination documented (chest auscultation findings); no SARS-CoV-2 test or influenza testing documented; no medication doses/routes/frequencies documented.
- Internal conflicts between transcript and DDx: none identified. (DDx suggestions were incorporated only where consistent with the transcript.)
- Transcript quality: adequate — clinician and patient exchanges generally clear; occasional conversational fillers but content intelligible and sufficient for documentation.
